According to the recycling review, a Li-ion cell's cathode is made up of active cathode material, conductive carbon, and binder, which are coated onto a current collector, namely Al foil. Active cathode materials (e.g., NMC622) account for around 30% of the cell weight.

According to the article on sustainable recycling of cathode scraps via Cyrene-based separation, the NMC622 recovered with Cyrene delivered a first charge capacity of 205.6 mAh/g, and the recovered NMC622 maintained 91.87% of the reversible discharge capacity.
